draft.title: Cosmic microwave background radiation
card: Cosmic microwave background radiation (CMB) is a faint glow of microwaves. It reaches Earth from every direction in space.
The CMB is leftover heat from the early universe. This heat was once much more intense.
As the universe expanded, this radiation was stretched out and cooled. Today it is in the microwave part of the spectrum.
The big bang theory says the early universe was hot and dense, and that it has been cooling since. The CMB matches this, so it supports the theory.
draft.remember: The CMB is cooled leftover heat from the early universe, and it supports the big bang theory.

a.q: What is the cosmic microwave background radiation?
opts: Cooled leftover heat from the early universe
Microwaves sent out by a single bright star
Radio signals made by the Milky Way's centre
Heat from stars that formed in recent times
a.why: The CMB is the cooled leftover heat of the early universe, and it reaches Earth from every direction. It does not come from one star or one galaxy, because it is spread across the whole sky.
a.clue: It comes from all directions, not one place.

b.q: Why do scientists say the CMB supports the big bang theory?
opts: It matches a hot early universe that has cooled
It shows that all stars are the same age
It proves that galaxies are moving apart
It comes from the one place where the bang happened
b.why: The big bang theory predicts a hot early universe that has cooled as it expanded, and the CMB is the glow left from that. It does not come from one place, because it arrives from every direction in space.
b.clue: Think about what the glow says about the early universe.

a.best: Cooled leftover heat from the early universe

b.best: It matches a hot early universe that has cooled
